2026-12-04.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Visitation · St John of Damascus
readings: Faith comes from what is heard
2026-12-04.alt: Mar Yohannan of Damascus (St John Damascene), monk of the Lavra of St Sabbas near Jerusalem, defender of holy icons, died around 749; Doctor of the Church. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-04.verse: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
theo: “So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.” Paul quotes Isaiah: God let himself be found by those who did not seek him. The word has gone out to the ends of the earth. St John of Damascus, whom we remember today, spent his life handing on that word faithfully; he also defended the holy icons, teaching that because the invisible God became visible in Christ, his face may be painted and venerated.

Jesus goes beneath the commandment “You shall not murder” to its root: anger and contempt. Whoever is angry with a brother or calls him a fool is already on the road to murder. And then a teaching for every worshipper: if at the altar you remember that your brother has something against you, “leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled”. Our offering at the Holy Qurbono is not acceptable while we refuse to be reconciled. A Friday of the fast is a good day to make peace.
outline: Is there anyone I need to make peace with before Christmas?
Jesus heals the heart, not only the hand.
The word reaches even those who did not seek.
“First be reconciled to your brother or sister.”
live: Take one step today toward reconciliation.
Pray before an icon of Christ or the Mother of God at home.
2026-12-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, you call us to be reconciled before we bring our gifts. Heal our anger, give us courage to make peace, and through the prayers of St John of Damascus, let us see your face. Amen.
altar: Before the anaphora we give the peace to one another. Reconciled, we offer the gifts and receive the Lord.

quick: Anger is the root of murder.
Be reconciled before you offer your gift.
Faith comes from hearing the word of Christ.
2026-12-04.action: Take one step today toward reconciliation.
2026-12-04.question: Whom must I be reconciled with before Christmas?

family.explain: Jesus says if we are angry with someone, we should make peace before we come to God's altar.
family.intention: We pray for peace in our family and with our neighbours.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to make peace with?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to be reconciled before we bring our gifts. As we gather, heal our anger and make us peacemakers. Amen.
share: Jesus warns against anger and insults (Matthew 5:22). When do I lose my temper?
Is there someone who has something against me?
What does the kiss of peace at the Holy Qurbono mean to me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us instruments of your peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a community of reconciliation.
For families divided by anger and quarrels.
For theologians and teachers of the faith, through the prayers of St John of Damascus.
For those who have not sought God, that he may find them.
For our group, that we may be at peace with one another.
pm.close: Lord God, through St John of Damascus you taught your Church to honour the image of your Son. Heal our anger and make us reconciled, so that our offering may please you. Amen.

illus: Two neighbours in Kottarakkara had fought over a boundary wall for years. One Friday, after the kiss of peace at the Qurbono, one of them walked over to the other's house. They are now godparents to each other's grandchildren.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember St John of Damascus, the great Syrian monk and teacher of the faith, who defended the holy icons and wrote beautiful hymns still sung in the Eastern Churches. He taught that because the invisible God became visible in Christ, we may honour images of Christ and his saints.

St Paul writes: faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ (Romans 10:17). Then he quotes Isaiah: I have been found by those who did not seek me (Romans 10:20). God's grace often reaches those we least expect.

In the Gospel Jesus deepens the commandment: you have heard that it was said, you shall not murder. But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgement (Matthew 5:21–22). Anger and insults are the roots of murder.

Then he says something very practical: if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled, and then come and offer your gift (Matthew 5:23–24).
In our Holy Qurbono we exchange the kiss of peace before the anaphora. This is the moment Jesus speaks of. It is not a formality; it is a commitment to be reconciled.
During this fast, let us look for one broken relationship and take a step towards peace: a phone call, a visit, an apology. Then our offering at Yaldo will be pleasing to God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: make peace first, then come to pray. If you had a fight with someone, say sorry today!

sub: Jesus names anger as liable to judgment.
q: Refrain from anger, and forsake wrath.
But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgment;
points.apply: Notice and offer to God one moment of anger today.

sub: Isaiah: cease to do evil, learn to do good.
q: cease to do evil, learn to do good;
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.

points.h: Found by those who did not seek
q: I was ready to be sought out by those who did not ask, to be found by those who did not seek me.
So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
points.apply: Listen to the Scripture readings at the next Qurbono with full attention.

concl: God first reconciled us to himself.
Let us carry that peace to others.
2026-12-04.resolve: Make peace with one person before Christmas.
